findings.issue: English Ellu Devarim is printed as two paragraphs but encoded as one tei:p with a literal newline inside it. TEI treats that newline as ordinary whitespace, so the printed break is lost.
findings.evidence: s47 band1: the line 'אלו The following matters have no legal measure:' is short and ends well before the right margin of the justified text (about x=1435 of 1670). The next line, 'The corner of the field…', starts at about x=207. That equals the first-line indent of the other p5 paragraphs (והערב about 185, ברוך about 200, יברכך about 200, אלהי about 210). Wrapped lines start at about x=160 ('the practice of charity…', 'to the following matters…'). So this is a new indented paragraph, not a wrap. The blind reader's note 'new line with no indent' is contradicted by the image; the enlarged reader's 'new indented line' is correct.
findings.fix: Split the EN unit into two tei:p: (1) 'The following matters have no legal measure:' and (2) 'The corner of the field, … with the study of Torah outweighing all of them.' Mirror this as en paragraph 1 and 2 in readings.json. Keep every word, the missing commas, 'study of the Torah' in the first sentence and 'study of Torah' in the last. HE stays one paragraph; do not force the two sides to match. Alignment is at the div level (prayer:ellu_devarim), so no milestone is needed.

findings.issue: The structural service file has a tei:bibl ptr but no biblScope. It carries printed content from p4 (the head, the p4 pb and the direction) and transcludes material running through p5.
findings.fix: Optional: add <tei:biblScope unit="pages" from="4" to="5"/> to both language files, unless the project convention is deliberately to leave biblScope off structural/index files.

alignment_findings.detail: HE: 10 tei:l, each opening with one of the ten stanza milestones (adon_olam … veim_ruchi), plus a bare stanza terminator in l10. EN: 12 tei:p carrying the same 10 milestones. Paragraph 8 ('The rock…') lies inside vehu_eli's scope and paragraph 12 ('God is with me…') inside veim_ruchi's, closed by the terminator. The paragraph counts were not forced to match.

HE l1 holds verses 24 and 25, l2 holds verse 26. EN is one p with three verse milestones. Both sides close with a bare verse terminator and a bare chapter terminator. No printed citation is invented. Note: the leading <milestone unit="chapter" n="6"/> has no corresp, so under rule 3 it is formally a terminator that closes nothing. It is harmless and consistent with the brief's 'excerpt context, not a whole-chapter witness'; I record it, not flag it.
Same div corresp on both sides; whole-prayer alignment. The EN Hebrew catchwords (ברוך, והערב, יברכך, אלו, אלהי, אדון) are correctly left out of the English prayer text.

Both files have the same transclusion order, matching the print: AdonOlam, Netilat, AsherYatzar, direction, Laasoq, Vehaarev, AsherBachar, Num6, EluDevarim, ElohaiNeshamah. Each has its own head (HE 'תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית.', EN 'Morning Prayer') after pb n=4. Both indexes transclude this file in the same place.
After the split, HE has 1 paragraph and EN 2. Alignment is unaffected.

remaining_source_ambiguities: Known and pending HUMAN (not re-raised as a finding): the pointing of והראיון in Ellu Devarim. The XML still holds the draft placeholder וְהָרֵאָיוֹן (tsere). The micro and tight crops show a vertically stacked pair under the resh, a horizontal stroke touching the heh's qamatz, and a single dot at the alef's upper left. Left unnormalized, as required.

Lowest-confidence item among the settled marks: the final-kaf interior dot in וִיחֻנֶּךָּ. The tight crop shows a mid-height round dot plus a separate low qamatz (medium-high confidence). The XML matches; this is noted only because it is the weakest of the settled readings.
